scorecard.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
scorecard.coaching: Acknowledge the customer's frustration before carrying on with the explanation, especially after they object to how they were spoken to.

scorecard.name: Paraphrasing
scorecard.coaching: You did not paraphrase or restate the customer's storm-related speed drop in your own words at any point in the call.

scorecard.name: Active listening
scorecard.coaching: The customer stated her street cabinet number at turn 7 (Cabinet 14), but at turn 37 you asked her again what street cabinet number she was connected to.

scorecard.name: Took ownership of the problem
scorecard.coaching: At turn 10, you deflected responsibility by stating lightning-induced speed drops on cabinet assets were not S-Net's responsibility.

scorecard.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
scorecard.coaching: At turn 32, you made a condescending and rude remark telling the customer that 'if you want gigabit lightning-proof reliability, you should pay for full fibre instead of complaining about copper'.

grader.scenario: Broadband sync speed dropped by half following Openreach cabinet lightning strike
grader.notes: Greg verifies security, acknowledges Lara's distress, and successfully resets the banded DLM profile on Cabinet 14 to restore sync from 36 Mbps back to 73 Mbps with live speed verification. However, he exhibits four distinct faults: he fails Paraphrasing, defers responsibility away from S-Net, makes a rude and condescending remark about complaining over copper, and repeats a question about the customer's cabinet number.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: At [08:01] the customer called the agent's remark rude and said full fibre is not available on her street; the agent replied 'As I said, copper lines pick up...' with no acknowledgement of her frustration.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Agent never restated the core issue in his own words; only confirmed email at turn 51.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [01:10] Customer: 'Our line connects to Openreach Cabinet 14 at the top of Church Lane.' followed by Agent at [07:20]: 'What was that street cabinet number in Matlock?'

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [01:45] Agent: 'Cabinet lightning strikes are entirely Openreach external physical assets, so speed drops aren't S-Net's responsibility.'

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [06:30] Agent: 'If you want gigabit lightning-proof reliability, you should pay for full fibre instead of complaining about copper.'
